title: st init: write a SIETCH marker-block into the rig's CLAUDE.md
description:
Sietch currently has no programmatic way to communicate framework-specific guidance to a Claude session running inside a consumer rig. A human Claude session has no idea that the dev-agent owns 'BRANCH_PREFIX/*' branches, that locks live under LOCK_DIR, or which 'st *' commands are available — it has to be told manually each time, or the user has to hand-write the same boilerplate into every rig's CLAUDE.md.

Mirror bd's pattern: a marker-bracketed block in CLAUDE.md, written by 'st init' and refreshed by a future 'st sync'. Closes the onboarding loop — 'st init' writes rig.config AND the CLAUDE.md block, so a new rig is genuinely one-step.
design:
New template: templates/claude-md-block.md — parameterized, rendered through the existing lib/render-prompt.sh pipeline.

bin/st cmd_init extended: after copying rig.config from the example, render claude-md-block.md and either:
  - append it to existing CLAUDE.md (between markers, preserving the rest), OR
  - write a new CLAUDE.md containing only the block + a stub heading

Hash computed by piping rendered block (without marker lines) into 'shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-8' and substituted into the BEGIN marker.

Idempotency: a small awk/sed pass detects the BEGIN/END pair. If present, skip; if absent, append. (Refresh-when-hash-stale is the 'st sync' job.)

Out of scope (file separately if/when needed):
  - 'st sync' to refresh the block on framework upgrade
  - Auto-detection of stale blocks across rigs
  - Per-rig customization of block content (beyond rig.config substitutions)
acceptance_criteria:
- 'st init' writes a SIETCH marker-block into the rig's CLAUDE.md
- Creates CLAUDE.md if it doesn't exist; preserves all user content outside the block if it does
- Idempotent: re-running 'st init' does not duplicate the block; if a block exists, leaves it alone (refresh is the future 'st sync' job)
- Marker format mirrors bd: <!-- BEGIN SIETCH INTEGRATION v:1 hash:<sha8> --> … <!-- END SIETCH INTEGRATION -->
- Block content includes:
  • one-paragraph mental model (this rig is a sietch consumer; framework lives at ~/code/sietch)
  • command reference (st dev / st review / st loop start / st help)
  • coordinate-with-dev-agent rules (don't push to BRANCH_PREFIX/*, don't tamper with LOCK_DIR, dev-agent uses filesystem locks for atomic claim)
  • pointer to .sietch/rig.config for tunables
- Block is parameterized — rig.config variables (BRANCH_PREFIX, LOCK_DIR, etc.) substituted via the existing render-prompt.sh
- Block hash is sha256 of rendered content truncated to 8 chars (used by future 'st sync' for drift detection)
- AGENTS.md is NOT touched — bd's choice to write to both files is a redundancy we don't repeat

title: add 'st permissions install' to bootstrap user-level Claude grants
description:
When a new user installs sietch, Claude Code re-prompts them for every Bash/MCP grant the agents need (gh, git, bd, python, pre-commit, tmux, …). A self-contained 'st permissions install' command should remove that friction so onboarding a rig is genuinely one-step.

Migrated from ai-cfo-eval-harness-a4fi (filed there before this repo had its own bd workspace).
design:
Subcommand 'permissions' added to bin/st with dispatch to lib/permissions.sh.

Grant list lives in lib/permissions.json — single source of truth, readable by users.
Scope = grants the four sietch agents actually invoke; NOT personal QoL:
  gh *, git *, bd *, st *, python *, python3 *, pytest *,
  pre-commit run *, ruff *, tmux *, pkill *, kill *, bash, jq *, mkdir *, chmod *

Implementation:
  - lib/permissions.sh reads lib/permissions.json (jq parses)
  - Reads existing ~/.claude/settings.json (creates from template if missing)
  - Computes set difference (new - existing) using jq
  - On install: cp settings.json settings.json.sietch.bak; jq merge writes new file
  - On --dry-run: print the diff list (one entry per line)
  - On list: cat lib/permissions.json | jq '.allow'
  - Atomic write: jq → temp file → mv into place

Out of scope (file separately if needed):
  - Project-specific grants (e.g. .venv/, PYTHONPATH=src) — those still belong in repo's .claude/settings.local.json
  - 'st permissions uninstall' (revert to backup) — nice-to-have, not in v1
  - Auto-running install during 'st init' — keep explicit; user opts in
acceptance_criteria:
- 'st permissions install' merges sietch-required grants into ~/.claude/settings.json
- Idempotent: re-running adds nothing if all entries already present (compare by exact string match)
- '--dry-run' prints the diff (entries that would be added) and exits 0 without writing
- 'st permissions list' prints the grant list as JSON (no I/O on settings.json)
- A backup is written to ~/.claude/settings.json.sietch.bak before any modification
- New ~/.claude/ is handled: creates settings.json with {permissions: {allow: [...]}} if missing
- JSON is validated (jq -e .) before and after; refuses to write if pre-state is invalid
- Clear error if jq is missing on PATH ('install jq via brew install jq')
- Top-level non-permission keys (e.g. effortLevel, skipAutoPermissionPrompt) are preserved
